summary: This standards-track document defines GMPLS OSPF-TE extensions for Flexi-Grid Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing networks. It follows the ITU-T flexible grid definitions in G.694.1 and G.872. The extensions let routers advertise the information needed for such optical networks.

plainLanguage.summary: Light in fiber can be split into many colors, and with flexi-grid each color gets the width it needs. This helps routers share information about those colors.

questions: how does ospf-te support flexi-grid dwdm
what is a flexi-grid optical network
what is the frequency availability bitmap
how does ospf-te advertise optical spectrum
subtitle: How OSPF-TE tells GMPLS routers which slices of an optical fiber's spectrum are still free.

tldr.problem: Flexi-grid optical links let each channel take a variable-width slice of frequency, so advertising a list of fixed wavelengths no longer describes what is free on a link.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds a new ISCD switching type (Flexi-Grid-LSC, 152) with a Frequency Availability Bitmap sub-TLV, and a flexi-grid restriction type for port label restrictions, all carried in OSPF-TE.
tldr.outcome: Path computation can learn which frequency ranges are available on each flexi-grid DWDM link and what slot widths each port supports.

today: RFC 8363 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 7698 and complements the signaling in RFC 7792.

sections.title: Why Flexi-Grid Needs New Routing Extensions
sections.content:
ITU-T Recommendation G.694.1 defines frequency grids for Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM). A fixed grid uses channel spacings from 12.5 GHz, 25 GHz, 50 GHz or 100 GHz up to integer multiples of 100 GHz. G.694.1 also defines a flexible grid, or flexi-grid, built on the ideas of a frequency slot (the range of frequency allocated to one channel) and a slot width.

RFC 7698 gives the framework for GMPLS control of flexi-grid networks, and RFC 7792 covers the RSVP-TE signaling. This RFC complements them by defining the OSPF-TE routing side.
sections.plainLanguage: Old fiber systems gave every color of light the same fixed lane. Flexi-grid lets each color pick a lane of the width it needs, so the routers need a new way to describe what is free.

sections.title: What Routing Must Advertise
sections.content:
A flexi-grid LSP occupies one or more frequency slots. Computing the route and assigning the slot is called Routing and Spectrum Assignment (RSA). With centralized spectrum assignment the chosen slot is named in the RSVP-TE Path message; with distributed assignment only the requested slot width is named and the nodes along the path pick the slot.

On a flexi-grid link, central frequencies step from 193.1 THz with 6.25 GHz granularity. Allocated slots on a link do not overlap, although the upper bound of one slot may equal the lower bound of the next. Because the slot width is not known until a slot is allocated, the routing protocol advertises available frequency ranges instead of individual wavelengths.

Devices may support only a subset of the possible positions and widths, so a flexi-grid link SHOULD also advertise the channel spacing (C.S., set to 5 to denote 6.25 GHz), the central frequency granularity, the slot width granularity and the slot width range.
sections.plainLanguage: Because lane widths vary, you cannot just say which numbered lanes are free. You have to say which stretches of the shelf are empty and how finely they can be cut.

sections.title: Fixed Grid Versus Flexi-Grid
sections.content:
On a fixed-grid link, each wavelength has a predefined central frequency and a usable range implied by the channel spacing. The wavelengths are identified by labels as defined in RFC 6205, and routing just advertises which are available.

On a flexi-grid link the slot width follows Slot Width (in GHz) = 12.5GHz * m, and m is uncertain until a slot is actually allocated. That is why the advertisement is built from the central frequency granularity and the slot width granularity rather than a list of fixed points.
sections.plainLanguage: A fixed grid is like a parking lot with painted spaces. Flexi-grid is a lot where the cars choose how much room they take.

sections.title: The ISCD and the Frequency Availability Bitmap
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new Switching Capability value for the Interface Switching Capability Descriptor (ISCD): 152, named Flexi-Grid-LSC, used with Encoding Type lambda. The ISCD is otherwise read as in RFC 4203, with optional Switching Capability Specific Information (SCSI) sub-TLVs. The generic Max LSP Bandwidth at priority x fields are not meaningful here, so they MUST be set to zero and MUST be ignored.

The flexi-grid SCSI is the Frequency Availability Bitmap sub-TLV, a new type of the Generalized SCSI TLV from RFC 8258. Its fields are:

  • Type (16 bits): 11.
  • Length (16 bits): length of the value in octets.
  • Priority (8 bits): which of priorities 0 to 7 are advertised; at least one MUST be, and a single one MUST be priority 0.
  • Max Slot Width at Priority k (16 bits each): largest slot width at that priority, in units of 2*C.S., one per set priority bit.
  • Unreserved Padding (16 bits): included when k is odd, omitted when even, to keep 32-bit alignment.
  • C.S. (4 bits): currently 5.
  • Starting n (16 bits): the first nominal central frequency in the bitmap.
  • No. of Effective Bits (12 bits): how many bitmap bits are meaningful.
  • Bitmap: one bit per basic slot (m of 1), 1 for available and 0 for unavailable.

A centralized spectrum assignment process must check enough consecutive available basic slots to build wider slots.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a row of tiny checkboxes, one per smallest slice of spectrum. A tick means the slice is free, and a header says where the row starts.

sections.title: A Worked Bitmap Example
sections.content:
The RFC uses a link whose supported range runs from n=-9 to n=11, with nominal central frequency 193.1 + n * 0.00625 THz. With Starting n set to -9 and 21 effective bits, the bitmap marks n=-1 to 7 as available.

The same availability can be expressed with Starting n set to -1 and 9 effective bits, all ones. If an LSP with m=1 is then set up at n=-1, the first bit flips to 0 and the advertisement is updated.
sections.plainLanguage: When someone takes one slice of the shelf, the router just flips that checkbox from tick to empty and tells its neighbors.

sections.title: Port Label Restrictions
sections.content:
A port may support only a subset of the full flexible grid. RFC 7579 defines the Port Label Restrictions field, carried in the top-level Link TLV as specified in RFC 7580. This RFC adds a flexi-grid Restriction Type, RstType = 5.

Besides MatrixID, the Switching Cap and Encoding (which MUST match the ISCD), it carries C.S. (5 for 6.25 GHz), C.F.G (central frequency granularity, a multiple of C.S.), S.W.G (slot width granularity, a multiple of 2*C.S.) and Min Slot Width (in multiples of 2*C.S.). Reserved fields MUST be zero on transmission.
sections.plainLanguage: Some ports can only handle certain slice sizes, like a toaster that fits only some bread. This field lists what each port can take.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA assigned value 152, Flexi-Grid-LSC, in the Switching Types sub-registry of the GMPLS Signaling Parameters registry. It also assigned Generalized SCSI TLV type 11, Frequency Availability Bitmap, for Switching Type 152.
sections.plainLanguage: The official number keeper wrote the new names and numbers into its list so everyone uses the same ones.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extensions carry flexi-grid information in OSPF Opaque LSAs and introduce no security issues beyond those in RFC 3630 and RFC 4203. The security mechanisms of RFC 2328 for Opaque LSAs still apply, and the OSPF security analysis in RFC 6863 applies to these extensions too.
sections.plainLanguage: The new messages ride in the same envelopes as before, so the old locks still protect them.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the value field in octets.

fields.name: Priority
fields.desc: Bitmap of advertised priority levels 0 to 7.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Zero on transmission, ignored on receipt.

fields.name: Starting n
fields.desc: Nominal central frequency of the first bitmap bit.

fields.name: No. of Effective Bits
fields.desc: Number of meaningful bits in the bitmap.
